questions.question: What does an empty user-item cell usually mean?
options: The preference is unknown or unexposed
The user definitely dislikes the item
The item is forbidden for every user
The matrix factor is mathematically zero in every trained model
questions.explanation: Missing feedback combines non-exposure, non-action, and unknown preference; it is not a confirmed negative.

questions.question: Why keep a popularity baseline?
options: It guarantees individual fairness
It is a strong, inspectable fallback and comparison
It removes exposure bias from historical data
It makes time-based evaluation unnecessary
questions.explanation: Popularity is simple and robust, especially for cold-start users, so personalization should beat it honestly.

questions.question: What does matrix factorization learn?
options: A separate hard-coded rule for every cell
Only global item counts
Latent vectors whose interaction estimates affinity
A guarantee that every unobserved item is irrelevant
questions.explanation: User and item latent vectors provide a compact representation whose dot product scores affinity.

questions.question: Which split best protects a next-item evaluation from future leakage?
options: Duplicate every interaction across train and test
Hold out later interactions per user
Choose test rows after fitting item popularity
Use only the users with the highest historical activity
questions.explanation: A per-user temporal or leave-last-out split better reproduces recommendation from past to future.

questions.question: Why can offline Recall@K improve while the product worsens?
options: Recall is always random
Ranked metrics cannot use held-out data
K must equal the entire catalog
Relevance can improve while diversity, safety, or long-term satisfaction declines
questions.explanation: Offline relevance covers only part of the product objective and can hide concentration or feedback-loop harms.

questions.question: What should a new-user fallback do?
options: Use an explicit eligible baseline such as recent popularity
Return latent-factor scores from an untrained user vector
Pretend every missing interaction is a negative rating
Reuse another user's private history without a policy
questions.explanation: An explicit, policy-compliant fallback is deterministic and inspectable when personalization has no evidence.
